findings: 2026-11-05: drafted for Mathematics 11 Unit 14 (owner request): English and a teacher-style Roman Urdu lesson; the book's content in order with our clearly labelled teaching notes; worked examples step by step with reasons; results verified with sympy.

Book correction: In Example 16 the book prints the unit vector as \frac{7\underline{i} - b\underline{j} - 10\underline{k}}{\sqrt{185}}. The middle term must be -6\underline{j}, from \underline{a} \times \underline{b} = 7\underline{i} - 6\underline{j} - 10\underline{k}: the correct unit vector is \frac{7\underline{i} - 6\underline{j} - 10\underline{k}}{\sqrt{185}}.

Book correction: In Example 17 the second bracket is printed (\cos\alpha\,\underline{i} + \sin\alpha\,\underline{i}); the second unit vector must be \underline{j}: \overrightarrow{OA} = \cos\alpha\,\underline{i} + \sin\alpha\,\underline{j}. The determinant that follows uses the correct components.
